issues.description: The problem statement and template expect Farm to initialize its internal ArrayList in a no-argument constructor (so code like 'new Farm()' in Main works), but the solution's Farm only provides a constructor with an int parameter (public Farm(int initialCapacity)) and no no-arg constructor. This constructor parameter mismatch breaks the explicit requirement and will cause code that instantiates Farm with 'new Farm()' to fail to compile or behave unexpectedly.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a no-argument constructor in Farm that initializes the animals list (e.g. public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }) or overload the existing constructor to include a no-arg version. Ensure the implementation matches the problem statement's explicit requirement for a constructor with no arguments.
